paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. God's judgments are just and true, and the singers say so before a single bowl is poured. They sing, "Great and wonderful are Your works, O Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the nations!" (Revelation 15:3). Later the angel of the waters and the altar say it too (Revelation 16:5-7).

Now look at the people on the receiving end. Three times they curse God, and the passage says they "did not repent" (Revelation 16:9, 11). I think that's the heaviest part of this whole chapter. The plagues were not the sad part, friend. The hard hearts were.

So where does that leave you and me? Right in the middle of the bowls, there's a word to the baker: "Behold, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who remains awake and clothed…" (Revelation 16:15). I never guess the day, because Matthew 24:36 says only the Father knows it. My job is to keep the ovens ready, and yours is to stay awake and clothed, friend, so let's keep baking.
